A.why: Huge square shoulder blocks and trouser legs under a near-white apron read as armour or a maid, not a flared gown.

B.why: A real flared moss skirt and black bodice, but the tall black shako headpiece and gold hip braid read as military or courtly, not forest.

C.why: The cleanest A-line skirt in the run, but a bare-looking yellow head from above, boxy sleeves and no moss or fungal frills.

D.why: A mushroom-cap hat and gill-ruffled tiered skirt that read as fungus from above, let down by a coat-like boxy bodice and a squat knee-length skirt.

E.why: A charming spotted mushroom cap on a stone-ziggurat skirt and wide one-green body that reads as a plinth more than a dress.

F.why: A nice fern crest, but a huge dark box chest on a stepped pyramid in a single green gives no waist and no femininity.

notes: No set yet has a narrow shoulder line. Every one keeps full-width block sleeves, so from the high camera the upper body is as wide as the hem. The moss, fungal-gill or fern frills of the brief show up only in D and E.
